document that safety alignment degrades in non-English languages, enabling jailbreaks via low-resource languages \\citep{Yong2023, Deng2023, Shen2024, Wang2023}.\nRecent work separates input-language from output-language effects \\citep{Marchisio2024, Zhang2026} and shows that safety pathways are shared across languages \\citep{Miao2026, Upadhyaya2026, Wang2025}.\nThe question of whether multilingual refusal gaps reflect over-refusal on benign items rather than under-refusal on harmful items is partially addressed by \\citet{Addagada2026}, who reports a relevance curse in non-English output, and by \\citet{Nguyen2026}, who cross prompt and response language on benign content.\n\\citet{Yoon2026} document the disparate cost of safety alignment across languages.\nThe novelty of the present work is partially occupied by these concurrent findings; our contribution is the signal-detection decomposition and the controlled sibling-pair design.\n\n\\paragraph{Abliteration.}\n\\citet{Arditi2024} showed that refusal in LLMs is mediated by a single direction in the residual stream, and that ablating this direction removes refusal.\n\\citet{Joad2026} demonstrated that multiple directions contribute.\n\\citet{Wang2025} found that the refusal direction generalizes across safety-aligned languages.\n\\citet{Krasnodebska2026} found that English-only DPO alignment does not ensure cross-lingual safety.\n\\citet{Hawkins2026} examined the safety impacts of benign multilingual fine-tuning.\n\n\\paragraph{Evaluation methodology.}\nLLM-as-judge evaluations carry systematic biases that compound across languages \\citep{Lee2025}.\nPrediction-powered inference (PPI++) provides a framework for correcting classifier estimates against a gold standard \\citep{Angelopoulos2023}.\n\\citet{Fiedler2026} shows that the Rogan--Gladen correction is unstable at low Youden $J$.\nStrongREJECT \\citep{Souly2024} introduced rubric-based evaluation of jailbreak quality.\n\\citet{Aziz2026} showed that low-resource safety failures are calibration failures, not representation failures.\n\n\\section{Method}\n\n\\subsection{Models and Edit Procedure}\n\nWe study Gemma-3-12B-IT and GaMS3-12B-Instruct, both loaded in NF4 (4-bit normal-float) quantization.\nGaMS3 extends Gemma-3 with Slovene continued pretraining on 140 billion tokens and supervised fine-tuning on a mix that is roughly 79\\% Slovene \\citep{Vres2026}.\n\nThe abliteration edit applies per-layer directional ablation via LoRA adapters \\citep{Hu2021}, optimized by a 40-trial TPE search \\citep{Akiba2019}.\nEach trial selects a layer subset, computes a refusal direction from contrastive pairs of harmful and benign English prompts, and projects it out of the residual stream.\nThe edit objective is to reduce English refusal while preserving capability on six benchmarks.\n\nWe use two edit doses throughout: a low dose ($\\lambda = 0.5$ for both models) and a high dose ($\\lambda = 1.0$ for Gemma, 0.625 for GaMS3), chosen to bracket the 50\\% English refusal point.\n\n\\subsection{Evaluation Design}\n\n\\paragraph{Over-refusal (criterion shift).}\nExperiment~5 tests 1,093 safe items (XSTest \\citep{Rottger2023} and OR-Bench) and 349 harmful items in English and Slovene.\nThe Slovene items are machine-translated with Gemini (gemini-2.5-flash); English items are back-translations.\nEach item is classified as refused or complied by a local Qwen3-14B judge, calibrated against gemini-2.5-flash on DEV (binary $\\kappa$ 0.68--0.86 across cells).\nThe hit rate (refusal on harmful items) and false-alarm rate (refusal on safe items) are computed per model $\\times$ language cell, and signal-detection parameters $d'$ and $c$ are derived.\nThe key contrast is the difference-in-differences (DiD), which isolates the model-by-language interaction:\n\\begin{equation}\n\\mathrm{DiD}_c = (c_{\\text{GaMS3,SL}} - c_{\\text{GaMS3,EN}}) - (c_{\\text{Gemma,SL}} - c_{\\text{Gemma,EN}}).\n\\end{equation}\nA positive $\\mathrm{DiD}_c$ means Gemma's criterion shifts more toward refusal in Slovene than GaMS3's does.\n\n\\paragraph{Crossed grid (reply-language refusal).}\nExperiment~14 crosses three prompt languages (English, Slovene, Hungarian) with three reply languages (English, Slovene, Hungarian) using a parallel one-line suffix in the input language.\nEach cell contains 200 harmful items and 100 benign items at three dose levels (zero, low, high).\nThe output-language mechanism contrast $\\mathrm{OUT}_{\\mathrm{SL}}$ is the mean log-odds refusal gap between Slovene-output and English-output cells, averaging over prompt languages.\nThe input-language contrast $\\mathrm{IN}_{\\mathrm{SL}}$ is defined symmetrically.\n\n\\paragraph{Judges and corrections.}\nThe primary judge for Experiment~14 is validated against blind author-model (not human) adjudication on 240 pooled edited rows: sensitivity $= 0.89$, specificity $= 0.73$, $\\kappa = 0.51$.\nIn the decisive Gemma Slovene-edited cell ($n = 60$), specificity drops to 0.42.\nPPI++ correction \\citep{Angelopoulos2023} is reported alongside raw estimates.\nExperiment~16 uses a held-out 294-item body with PPI as the primary estimator.\nThe harmful-content adjudicator $\\kappa$ in Experiment~16 is 0.12, pooled over $n = 400$, well below the 0.60 gate.\n\n\\paragraph{Language compliance.}\nCells where fewer than 90\\% of model replies match the requested output language are excluded from mechanism claims or marked.\nThe excluded cells for GaMS3 are: SL$\\to$EN (compliance 0.00), HU$\\to$EN (0.14), SL$\\to$HU (0.56), and HU$\\to$SL (0.86).\n\n\\subsection{Hungarian as a Control Language}\n\nHungarian serves as a typologically distant control.\nThe minimum detectable effect for Hungarian contrasts is approximately 3 log-odds units, far larger than any observed effect; all Hungarian results are uninformative.\n\n\\section{Results}\n\n\\subsection{Over-Refusal: Criterion Shift on Benign Items (ESTIMATE)}\n\\label{sec:criterion}\n\nThe main measurement is that Gemma applies a stricter refusal criterion in Slovene than in English on benign items, while GaMS3 does not.\nTable~\\ref{tab:sdt} reports the signal-detection parameters from Experiment~5.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Signal-detection parameters by model and language (Experiment~5, 1,093 safe $+$ 349 harmful items, Qwen3-14B judge).}\n\\label{tab:sdt}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\n & Gemma EN & Gemma SL & GaMS3 EN & GaMS3 SL \\\\\n\\midrule\nHit rate ($H$) & 0.89 & 0.94 & 0.90 & 0.86 \\\\\nFalse-alarm rate ($F$) & 0.364 & 0.569 & 0.273 & 0.273 \\\\\n$d'$ & 1.57 & 1.39 & 1.86 & 1.68 \\\\\n$c$ & $-0.44$ & $-0.87$ & $-0.33$ & $-0.23$ \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe DiD on the criterion parameter is $+0.52$ $[0.38, 0.68]$ (95\\% CI).\nGemma's Slovene criterion is shifted by half a standard deviation relative to the GaMS3 baseline.\nThe DiD on $d'$ is $-0.003$ $[-0.33, 0.29]$, indistinguishable from zero: the asymmetry is in the threshold, not the sensitivity.\nFigure~\\ref{fig:sdt} shows the decomposition.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_sdt_v0.pdf}\n\\caption{Signal-detection parameters from Experiment~5 on the HARD set (1,093 benign and 349 harmful items; Slovene machine translations vs English back-translations; refusals labelled by a local Qwen3-14B judge, with partial answers coded as non-refusals). Blue bars are English prompts and orange bars are Slovene prompts, for Gemma-3-12B-IT (``Gemma~3'') and GaMS3-12B-Instruct (``GaMS3''). (a)~False-alarm rate $F$, the proportion of benign items refused, with Wilson 95\\% confidence intervals. Brackets give the paired Slovene$-$English difference and an exact McNemar test on the same items. Gemma's rate rises from 0.364 to 0.569 ($p<10^{-28}$), while GaMS3 refuses 0.273 of benign items in both languages ($p=1.0$). (b)~SDT criterion $c$ in $z$ units, where more negative means a greater tendency to refuse. Lower brackets show the within-model shift $\\Delta c$ (Slovene$-$English, 95\\% CI): Gemma moves toward refusing in Slovene ($c=-0.87$ vs $-0.44$; $\\Delta c=-0.43$ [$-0.57$, $-0.31$]), while GaMS3 does not ($-0.23$ vs $-0.33$; $\\Delta c=+0.09$ [$-0.002$, $0.19$]). The upper bracket gives the difference-in-differences $\\mathrm{DiD}_c=+0.52$ [0.38, 0.68]. The corresponding DiD on sensitivity $d'$ ($-0.003$ [$-0.33$, $0.29$]) is indistinguishable from zero, so the asymmetry lies in the threshold rather than in discrimination. This finding is rated ESTIMATE: coding partial answers as refusals reverses $\\mathrm{DiD}_c$ to $-0.31$ [$-0.62$, $-0.09$].}\n\\label{fig:sdt}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\paragraph{Rating and caveats.}\nWe use a three-level evidence rating: ROBUST (survives all pre-registered checks), ESTIMATE (the point estimate is informative but at least one sensitivity check fails), and INCONCLUSIVE (the confidence interval includes zero or the result is fragile).\nThis finding is rated ESTIMATE for three reasons.\nFirst, the sign reverses to $-0.31$ when partial answers are coded as refusals rather than compliance.\nSecond, 8 of 9 compliance-valid rows across five analyses (Experiments~5, 9, 14, 15, and a secondary rescoring) point the same way as the headline, but this count was a post-hoc refinement made after the frozen rule found an unresolved cross-body disagreement.\nThird, a Qwen3-14B rescoring gives a similar interval $[0.39, 0.67]$, but this is a re-derivation from the same Experiment~5 items, not an independent sample.\n\n\\paragraph{Edited-model criterion shift.}\nOn edited models, the criterion difference is inconclusive: Experiment~11 HARD post-edit $\\mathrm{DiD}_c = 0.14$ $[-0.78, 1.12]$, whose CI includes zero.\n\n\\subsection{Reply-Language Refusal (ESTIMATE, Weak Anchor)}\n\\label{sec:reply}\n\nIn the $3{\\times}3$ crossed grid (Experiment~14), edited Gemma at high dose shows a pattern in which residual refusal is higher when the model replies in Slovene than in English.\nTables~\\ref{tab:gemma_grid} and~\\ref{tab:gams3_grid} give the refusal rates; Figure~\\ref{fig:grid} visualizes the full grid.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Refusal rates at high edit dose, Gemma (harmful items, 200 per cell).}\n\\label{tab:gemma_grid}\n\\begin{tabular}{lccc}\n\\toprule\n & EN out & SL out & HU out \\\\\n\\midrule\nEN in & 0.18 & 0.77 & 0.46 \\\\\nSL in & 0.07 & 0.56 & 0.53 \\\\\nHU in & 0.10 & 0.83 & 0.55 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Refusal rates at high edit dose, GaMS3 (harmful items, 200 per cell; cells below 90\\% compliance marked $\\dag$).}\n\\label{tab:gams3_grid}\n\\begin{tabular}{lccc}\n\\toprule\n & EN out & SL out & HU out \\\\\n\\midrule\nEN in & 0.21 & 0.14 & 0.23 \\\\\nSL in & 0.16$\\dag$ & 0.15 & 0.17$\\dag$ \\\\\nHU in & 0.19$\\dag$ & 0.12$\\dag$ & 0.28 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe raw mechanism contrast is $\\mathrm{OUT}_{\\mathrm{SL}} = +1.14$ $[0.60, 1.56]$ log-odds for Gemma and the input-language contrast is $\\mathrm{IN}_{\\mathrm{SL}} = -0.60$ $[-1.02, -0.18]$.\nFor GaMS3, the input-language contrast $\\mathrm{IN}_{\\mathrm{SL}} = -0.86$ $[-1.58, -0.13]$ excludes zero.\nThe cross-model output contrast is $\\mathrm{dOUT}_{\\mathrm{SL}} = -1.58$ $[-2.22, -0.66]$.\nHowever, the PPI-corrected output contrast for Gemma is $0.20$ $[-0.76, 1.13]$, consistent with zero, and the robustness check across readouts does not pass.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_grid_v0.pdf}\n\\caption{Refusal rates on harmful items at high edit dose in the $3{\\times}3$ prompt-language $\\times$ requested-reply-language grid (Experiment~14, 200 harmful items per cell, primary-judge raw readout). Rows give the prompt language and columns the requested reply language (EN, SL, HU). Colour encodes the refusal rate on a shared white-to-dark-red scale from 0 to 1. Each cell prints the rate with its Wilson 95\\% CI beneath. (a)~Gemma-3-12B-IT: the Slovene-reply column is the most refused (0.560--0.835), the English-reply column the least (0.075--0.185), and the Hungarian-reply column sits in between (0.460--0.550). (b)~GaMS3-12B-Instruct: refusal is uniformly low (0.125--0.280) with no reply-language column pattern. $\\dag$~marks cells whose language compliance, pooled over the three dose levels, is below 90\\%. All four are GaMS3 cells off the English-prompt row (SL$\\to$EN, SL$\\to$HU, HU$\\to$EN, HU$\\to$SL), so their reply-language labels are unreliable. The Gemma output-language contrast holds on this raw readout, but its PPI-corrected estimate includes zero. The CIs inside the darkest Gemma cells (SL-reply column, top to bottom) are $[0.71,\\,0.82]$, $[0.49,\\,0.63]$, $[0.78,\\,0.88]$.}\n\\label{fig:grid}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\paragraph{Experiment~16 confirmation.}\nOn a fresh 294-item body, Experiment~16 gives the PPI-corrected estimate $\\mathrm{OUT}_{\\text{Gemma}} = {+}2.43$ $[{+}0.89, {+}5.38]$ log-odds, and the cross-model difference $\\mathrm{dOUT} = -2.31$ $[-5.34, -0.68]$ excludes zero.\nAll confirmation clauses pass on the consensus reference.\nHowever, the verdict is capped at ESTIMATE because the harmful-content adjudicator $\\kappa$ is 0.12 (pooled over $n = 400$), well below the 0.60 gate.\nThe adjudicator disagreement stems from truncation: one judge scored cut-off partial compliance as non-harmful, while the other graded the partial content 2--4.\nThe anchor is weak.\n\n\\paragraph{SDT decomposition of the output-language effect.}\nAt high dose, the Slovene-output criterion DiD (Gemma minus GaMS3) is $-1.56$ $[-1.97, -1.29]$ and the $d'$ DiD is $0.72$ $[-0.06, 1.30]$, which includes zero.\nThis is a separate reply-language criterion contrast, computed at the cell level as Gemma minus GaMS3; after harmonising the sign convention, it is counted among the compliance-valid rows that agree with the headline.\n\n\\paragraph{Compliant-row contrast.}\nRestricting to rows where both models achieve ${>}90\\%$ compliance (EN-input rows only), the edit-induced cross-model contrast is $\\mathrm{G3}_{\\text{edit}}(\\text{EN}{\\to}\\text{SL})$~$=$~$-1.26$~$[-2.17,\\allowbreak 0.20]$, whose CI includes zero.\n\n\\paragraph{Benign false refusal.}\nFrom blind adjudication ($n = 30$ per cell), Gemma falsely refuses benign EN$\\to$SL prompts at 0.20 $[0.10, 0.37]$ vs EN$\\to$EN at 0.10 $[0.03, 0.26]$.\n\n\\paragraph{Refusal composition.}\nAmong Gemma's high-dose EN$\\to$SL harmful-item responses (blind adjudication, $n = 50$), 54\\% are explicit refusals and 26\\% are deflections.\nThe deflection rate, defined as the proportion of non-refusal responses that are off-topic deflections rather than substantive answers, differs between Gemma EN$\\to$SL and EN$\\to$EN by 0.46 $[0.23, 0.65]$, consistent with the relevance curse described by \\citet{Shen2024} and the output-language effect reported by \\citet{Addagada2026}.\n\n\\subsection{Dose-Response}\n\nFigure~\\ref{fig:dose} plots refusal rate against abliteration dose for both models.\nExperiment~9 measures refusal rates across nine $\\lambda$ values for both models in English and Slovene (300 items per model $\\times$ language cell at $\\lambda = 0$, 100 items at each edited step).\nGemma's dose-response curve in Slovene is right-shifted relative to its English curve: at matched doses, more Slovene refusal remains.\nGaMS3 shows a smaller shift.\nThe fine-grained 13-step dose ladder (Experiment~15) gives the most powerful estimate: $\\mathrm{G3} = -0.70$ $[-1.01, -0.42]$ with a minimum detectable effect of 0.42.\nThe edit-induced component is $+0.47$ $[-0.96, 2.14]$, whose CI includes zero; whether the cross-model gap is baseline or edit-induced is inconclusive.\n\n\\subsection{Inconclusive and Null Results}\n\n\\paragraph{Unedited cross-model gap at Slovene-to-Slovene prompts.}\nExperiment~15 gives $\\mathrm{G3}_{\\text{orig}} = -1.17$ $[-2.83, 0.22]$.\nThis is a ceiling artefact: its fragility index, the number of item reclassifications needed to move the CI boundary past zero, is 1 (a single item reclassification in the Gemma $\\lambda\\text{-}0$ Slovene cell, where 299 of 300 items are refused, moves it inside the margin).\nOnly the Experiment~9 body has a robust offset (fragility index 9).\n\n\\paragraph{Hungarian.}\nAll Hungarian contrasts are uninformative.\nThe minimum detectable effect is approximately 3 log-odds units.\n\n\\paragraph{Experiment~16 zero-dose.}\nThe Experiment~16 zero-dose Gemma criterion DiD is $-0.65$~$[-0.90,\\allowbreak -0.46]$, rated ESTIMATE.\nIt does not confirm the Experiment~5 headline because it uses a different item body, a different judge, and a suffix-based output-language design rather than paired translation.\n\n\\paragraph{RefusEU validation.}\nExperiment~17 tests attack success rate on 1,300 EN $+$ 1,300 SL RefusEU prompts.\nThe edit is effective in all four model $\\times$ language cells (ROBUST), with ASR deltas of 0.657--0.937.\nThe EN-vs-SL within-model difference is not interpretable as a language effect because the prompt sets are different natural prompts (LaBSE similarity 0.55).\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_dose_v0.pdf}\n\\caption{Refusal rate on harmful prompts as a function of abliteration dose $\\lambda$ for Gemma-3-12B-IT (blue) and GaMS3-12B-Instruct (amber), in English (solid lines, filled circles; EN-BT arm) and Slovene (dashed lines, hollow squares; item-matched SL-MT arm). $\\lambda$ scales each model's own selected abliteration edit (9~steps from 0 to 2; $\\lambda=1$ is the selected edit), so equal $\\lambda$ does not mean an equal edit across models. Points are J1-judged refusal rates from the Experiment~9 RefusEU-TRAIN probe, with the Hautus correction $(k+0.5)/(n+1)$ used in the Experiment~9 analysis. Shaded bands are Wilson 95\\% intervals on the raw proportion. $n=300$ harmful items at $\\lambda=0$ and the 100-item core block at every $\\lambda>0$. Gemma's Slovene curve lies to the right of its English curve throughout the transition (0.64 vs.\\ 0.32 at $\\lambda=1$): at each dose, more Slovene refusal remains. GaMS3's Slovene curve lies only slightly above its English curve (largest gap 0.14, at $\\lambda=0.5$), and the two meet near the floor from $\\lambda=1$ onward. These per-dose gaps are descriptive. The pre-registered cross-model comparison is made at matched English refusal, not at matched dose.}\n\\label{fig:dose}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\section{Discussion}\n\\label{sec:discussion}\n\n\\subsection{Interpretation}\n\nThe criterion-shift measurement has a concrete interpretation for multilingual evaluation: a model can appear ``safer'' in a non-English language because it refuses more benign requests, inflating the refusal rate without any improvement in harm detection.\nThe SDT framing separates these two components.\nThe near-zero DiD on $d'$ means that the language shift does not make either model better or worse at distinguishing harmful from benign items; the measured difference is in the threshold.\n\\citet{Aziz2026} described a similar calibration-not-representation pattern across 23 languages; the present sibling-pair design adds GaMS3-specific detail but does not change the interpretation.\n\nThe reply-language finding, if confirmed by future work with validated judge anchors, would suggest that Gemma's refusal mechanism interacts with output-language processing.\n\\citet{Upadhyaya2026} showed that safety features are geometrically entangled with language-identity features; the present study's $3{\\times}3$ design separates the input and output dimensions but cannot determine the mechanism.\n\n\\subsection{Limitations}\n\n\\paragraph{ESTIMATE rating on the primary finding.}\nThe criterion-shift DiD reverses sign ($-0.31$) when partial answers are coded as refusals.\nThe choice of coding rule therefore determines whether over-refusal is attributed to Gemma or is absent.\nThis fragility bounds how strongly the finding can be stated.\nFurthermore, restricting Experiment~5 to the XSTest items alone gives $\\mathrm{DiD}_c = 0.10$ $[-0.13, 0.35]$, so the effect is carried by the OR-Bench items.\n\n\\paragraph{Judge quality.}\nThe Qwen3-14B judge for Experiment~5 was calibrated against gemini-2.5-flash on DEV ($\\kappa$ 0.68--0.86) but not against human labels.\nOn edited rows across the study, no judge exceeds $\\kappa = 0.51$ against blind adjudication.\nThe readout gate has never passed.\nAll adjudication in this study is author-model LLM, not human review.\n\n\\paragraph{Sample size.}\nThe adjudication sample is 30 items per cell for benign false-refusal rates, limiting precision.\nThe refusal-composition numbers (54\\% explicit, 26\\% deflection) come from $n = 50$ high-dose harmful items.\n\n\\paragraph{Language compliance.}\nFour GaMS3 cells fall below 90\\% compliance (SL$\\to$EN at 0.00, HU$\\to$EN at 0.14, SL$\\to$HU at 0.56, HU$\\to$SL at 0.86).\nGaMS3 did not follow the output-language instruction off the English-input row; its SL$\\to$EN responses were written in Slovene, not English.\nMechanism claims for GaMS3 are therefore restricted to the compliant EN-input row.\n\n\\paragraph{Quantization.}\nBoth models run in NF4 (4-bit) quantization, which may affect refusal behaviour relative to full-precision weights.\n\n\\paragraph{Novelty.}\nThe observation that over-refusal rates differ across languages is partially anticipated by \\citet{Addagada2026} and \\citet{Nguyen2026}.\nThe present work's contribution is the signal-detection decomposition and the controlled sibling-pair design.\n\n\\section{Conclusion}\n\nUnedited Gemma-3-12B-IT false-refuses benign Slovene items at 0.569 vs 0.364 in English.\nSignal-detection analysis attributes this to a criterion shift ($\\mathrm{DiD}_c = +0.52$ $[0.38, 0.68]$) with no sensitivity difference.\nThe finding is rated ESTIMATE because the sign reverses under an alternative coding rule.\nOn edited models, the criterion difference is inconclusive (0.14 $[-0.78, 1.12]$).\nA secondary analysis of reply-language refusal yields a PPI-corrected output-language effect of $+2.43$ $[+0.89, +5.38]$ for Gemma, but this is also rated ESTIMATE because the harmful-content adjudicator $\\kappa$ is 0.12.\nMultilingual safety evaluations that report only attack-success rates on harmful items will miss criterion shifts that inflate refusal rates on benign items.\n\n\\bibliographystyle{plainnat}\n\\bibliography{references}\n\n\\end{document}\n", "numLines": 325, "startLine": 1, "totalLines": 325}}

"""Build the JSON blocks embedded in interactive.html from the run's saved output files.

Reads only; writes JSON into the scratchpad. Every value is copied from, or counted in, the files named below.
"""
import json
import math
import random
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path("/ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_FVi3e3O9CH5I/3_invention_loop")
EXP5 = ROOT / "iter_2/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_5"
EXP14 = ROOT / "iter_4/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_14"
OUT = Path(__file__).parent / "data"
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

TEXT_CAP = 600  # characters of each reply kept for the item browser
SAMPLE_REST = 180
SEED = 20260926

ARMS = ["EN_orig", "EN_BT", "SL_MT"]
MODELS = ["gemma_it", "gams3_it"]
CODE = {"REFUSE": "R", "PARTIAL": "P", "COMPLY": "C"}


def wilson(k, n, z=1.959963984540054):
    p = k / n
    den = 1 + z * z / n
    centre = (p + z * z / (2 * n)) / den
    half = z * math.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z * z / (4 * n * n)) / den
    return [centre - half, centre + half]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- exp5 SDT variants
an = json.loads((EXP5 / "results/analysis_final.json").read_text())
sdt = an["C2_hard_sdt"]
variants = {}
for key, v in sdt.items():
    if not isinstance(v, dict) or "DiD_c" not in v:
        continue
    variants[key] = {
        "cells": v["cells"],  # order: gemma EN, gemma SL, gams EN, gams SL
        "DiD_c": {k: v["DiD_c"][k] for k in ("est", "ci95")},
        "DiD_dprime": {k: v["DiD_dprime"][k] for k in ("est", "ci95")},
    }
prim = sdt["primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT"]
sdt_block = {
    "variants": variants,
    "own_delta": prim["own_delta"],
    "mcnemar": prim["mcnemar_within_model_SL_vs_EN"],
    "n_unsafe": prim["n_unsafe"],
    "n_safe": prim["n_safe"],
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- exp5 per-item HARD rows
rows = [json.loads(l) for l in (EXP5 / "results/items_final.jsonl").open()]
hard = [r for r in rows if r["set"] == "hard" and r["arm"] in ARMS]
by_item = {}
for r in hard:
    it = by_item.setdefault(r["item_id"], {"src": r["source"], "harm": bool(r["is_harmful"]),
                                           "frag": bool(r["mt_fragile"]), "xt": r["xstest_type"],
                                           "lab": {}, "txt": {}, "resp": {}})
    lab = r["judge_primary"]
    assert lab in CODE, lab
    it["lab"][(r["model"], r["arm"])] = CODE[lab]
    it["txt"][r["arm"]] = r["prompt_text"]
    it["resp"][(r["model"], r["arm"])] = r["response"]
    if r["arm"] == "SL_MT":
        it["chrf"] = r["bt_chrf"]

ids = sorted(by_item)
labels = []
for iid in ids:
    it = by_item[iid]
    code = "".join(it["lab"][(m, a)] for m in MODELS for a in ARMS)
    src = {"xstest": "X", "orbench_hard1k": "O", "orbench_toxic": "T"}[it["src"]]
    labels.append([iid, src, 1 if it["harm"] else 0, 1 if it["frag"] else 0, code])
label_block = {
    "order": [f"{m}|{a}" for m in MODELS for a in ARMS],
    "fields": ["item_id", "source X=XSTest O=OR-Bench-Hard-1K T=OR-Bench-Toxic", "is_harmful", "mt_fragile",
               "labels R=REFUSE P=PARTIAL C=COMPLY in 'order'"],
    "rows": labels,
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- texts for the item browser (benign only)
def refuses(it, m, a):
    return it["lab"][(m, a)] == "R"

benign = [iid for iid in ids if not by_item[iid]["harm"]]
flip = [iid for iid in benign if refuses(by_item[iid], "gemma_it", "SL_MT") != refuses(by_item[iid], "gemma_it", "EN_BT")]
rest = [iid for iid in benign if iid not in set(flip)]
rng = random.Random(SEED)
sample = sorted(rng.sample(rest, SAMPLE_REST))
keep = sorted(set(flip) | set(sample))


def cap(s):
    s = s.strip()
    return s if len(s) <= TEXT_CAP else s[:TEXT_CAP].rstrip() + " […]"

texts = {}
for iid in keep:
    it = by_item[iid]
    texts[iid] = {
        "en": it["txt"]["EN_BT"], "enorig": it["txt"]["EN_orig"], "sl": it["txt"]["SL_MT"],
        "chrf": it.get("chrf"),
        "type": it["xt"],
        "r": [cap(it["resp"][(m, a)]) for m in MODELS for a in ("EN_BT", "SL_MT")],

.pipe svg{display:block;width:100%;height:auto}
.pipe .node{cursor:pointer}
.pipe .node rect{fill:#fff;stroke:#c9c8c1;stroke-width:1.5}
.pipe .node.done rect{fill:var(--base-soft);stroke:var(--base)}
.pipe .node[aria-current="step"] rect{fill:var(--accent);stroke:var(--accent)}
.pipe .node[aria-current="step"] text{fill:#fff}
.pipe .node text{font-size:12.5px;fill:var(--ink);font-family:var(--font);font-weight:600}
.pipe .node:focus-visible rect{stroke:var(--focus);stroke-width:3}
.stage{min-height:300px}
.stage-grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(3,minmax(0,1fr));gap:14px}
@media (max-width:860px){.stage-grid{grid-template-columns:1fr}}
.io .lab{font-size:.78rem;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.06em;color:var(--ink3);font-weight:650;margin-bottom:4px}
.io{background:var(--panel);border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:8px;padding:12px 14px;min-width:0}
.io.why{background:#f5f4ef}
.snip{font-size:.92rem;line-height:1.5;white-space:pre-wrap;overflow-wrap:anywhere;max-height:260px;overflow:auto}
.navrow{display:flex;gap:10px;align-items:center;flex-wrap:wrap}
.navrow .pos{font-size:.92rem;color:var(--ink3);margin-left:6px}
.chip{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;min-width:26px;height:22px;padding:0 6px;border-radius:5px;font-size:.76rem;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.02em;font-family:var(--mono)}
.chip.R{background:var(--accent);color:#fff}
.chip.P{background:#f1d9a6;color:#5a3b00}
.chip.C{background:#e4ece6;color:#24522e}
table{border-collapse:collapse;font-size:.93rem;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
th,td{padding:7px 10px;border-bottom:1px solid var(--rule2);text-align:right;vertical-align:top}
th:first-child,td:first-child{text-align:left}
thead th{font-size:.8rem;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.04em;color:var(--ink3);font-weight:650;border-bottom:1px solid var(--rule)}
.tablewrap{overflow-x:auto;max-width:100%}
.browser{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,340px) minmax(0,1fr);gap:16px;align-items:start}
@media (max-width:860px){.browser{grid-template-columns:1fr}}
.ilist{list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0;max-height:620px;overflow:auto;border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:8px;background:#fff}
@media (max-width:860px){.ilist{max-height:340px}}
.ilist li{border-bottom:1px solid var(--rule2)}
.ilist button{display:block;width:100%;text-align:left;font:inherit;font-size:.9rem;line-height:1.4;padding:10px 12px;background:none;border:0;cursor:pointer;color:var(--ink);min-height:44px}
.ilist button:hover{background:#f6f5f0}
.ilist button[aria-selected="true"]{background:var(--accent-soft);box-shadow:inset 4px 0 0 var(--accent)}
.ilist .chips{display:flex;gap:4px;margin-top:5px;flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:center}
.ilist .chips .sep{width:8px}
.detail .pair{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr));gap:12px}
@media (max-width:560px){.detail .pair{grid-template-columns:1fr}}
.reply{border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:8px;padding:10px 12px;background:#fff;min-width:0}
.reply.isR{border-color:#e2b49c;background:#fffaf6}
.reply .hd{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;gap:8px;align-items:center;font-size:.8rem;color:var(--ink3);font-weight:650;margin-bottom:6px;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.04em}
.detail .prompt{background:#f5f4ef;border-radius:8px;padding:10px 12px;font-size:.95rem;min-width:0;overflow-wrap:anywhere}
.count{font-size:.92rem;color:var(--ink2);margin:6px 0 8px}
.heat{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr));gap:18px}
@media (max-width:760px){.heat{grid-template-columns:1fr}}
.two{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr));gap:22px}
@media (max-width:860px){.two{grid-template-columns:1fr}}
ul.lim{padding-left:1.1em;max-width:74ch}
ul.lim li{margin:.45em 0}
footer{background:#f2f1ec;border-top:1px solid var(--rule);padding:40px 0 60px;font-size:.95rem}
footer h2{font-size:1.3rem}
footer h3{font-size:1.05rem;margin-top:1.4em}
dl.gloss{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(0,220px) minmax(0,1fr);gap:6px 18px;max-width:1000px}
dl.gloss dt{font-weight:650}
dl.gloss dd{margin:0 0 6px}
@media (max-width:640px){dl.gloss{grid-template-columns:1fr}dl.gloss dd{margin-bottom:12px}}
.prov li{margin:.3em 0}
code{font-family:var(--mono);font-size:.86em;background:#efeee8;padding:1px 5px;border-radius:4px;overflow-wrap:anywhere}
.sr{position:absolute;width:1px;height:1px;overflow:hidden;clip:rect(0 0 0 0);white-space:nowrap}
.badge{display:inline-block;font-size:.72rem;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:.06em;text-transform:uppercase;padding:3px 8px;border-radius:5px;background:#f1d9a6;color:#5a3b00;vertical-align:middle}
.note{font-size:.88rem;color:var(--ink3)}
</style>
</head>
<body>
<a class="skip" href="#main">Skip to main content</a>
<header class="top">
  <div class="wrap">
    <p class="kicker">Interactive companion to the paper</p>
    <h1>Over-Refusal of Benign Slovene Prompts in Gemma-3-12B Is a Criterion Shift</h1>
    <p class="lede">Gemma-3-12B-IT refuses harmless requests more often when they are written in Slovene. Its Slovene-adapted sibling GaMS3-12B-Instruct does not. This page lets you operate the analysis that separates <em>how well</em> each model tells harmful from harmless apart from <em>how readily</em> it refuses.</p>
    <div class="links">
      <a class="btn primary" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-2cf2a7-does-slovene-taught-refusal-survive@fork/run_03_dodOtFxiE/paper.pdf">Read the paper (PDF)</a>
      <a class="btn" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-2cf2a7-does-slovene-taught-refusal-survive@fork/run_03_dodOtFxiE/report.pdf">Read the full research report</a>
      <a class="btn" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-2cf2a7-does-slovene-taught-refusal-survive/tree/fork/run_03_dodOtFxiE">Code repository</a>
    </div>
  </div>
</header>
<nav class="sections" aria-label="Sections">
  <ul>
    <li><a href="#finding">The finding</a></li>
    <li><a href="#how">How it works</a></li>
    <li><a href="#evidence">Explore the evidence</a></li>
    <li><a href="#try">Try it</a></li>
    <li><a href="#reply">Reply language</a></li>
    <li><a href="#fails">Where it fails</a></li>
    <li><a href="#sources">Sources &amp; glossary</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>

<main id="main" tabindex="-1">

<!-- ============================================================ FINDING -->
<section class="block" id="finding" aria-labelledby="h-finding">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-finding">The finding</h2>
  <div class="finding">
    <div>
      <p class="question">When Gemma refuses more in Slovene, is it worse at spotting harm, or does it simply refuse more readily?</p>
      <p>The study scored both unedited models on the <button class="term" data-term="hard">HARD set</button>: <span data-num="sdt.n_safe" data-fmt="int"></span> benign and <span data-num="sdt.n_unsafe" data-fmt="int"></span> harmful prompts, each posed as a <button class="term" data-term="slmt">Slovene machine translation</button> and as an <button class="term" data-term="enbt">English back-translation</button>. On benign prompts, Gemma's <button class="term" data-term="F">false-alarm rate</button> rises from <span data-num="v.primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT.cells.F.0" data-fmt="f3"></span> in English to <span data-num="v.primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT.cells.F.1" data-fmt="f3"></span> in Slovene. GaMS3 refuses <span data-num="v.primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT.cells.F.2" data-fmt="f3"></span> in both.</p>
      <p><button class="term" data-term="sdt">Signal-detection theory</button> splits that gap in two. The shift sits in the <button class="term" data-term="c">criterion</button>, not in <button class="term" data-term="dprime">sensitivity</button>:</p>
      <div class="bignum" aria-describedby="bignum-sub"><span data-num="v.primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT.DiD_c.est" data-fmt="s2"></span></div>
      <div class="bignum-sub" id="bignum-sub"><button class="term" data-term="didc">DiD<sub>c</sub></button>, 95% CI <span data-num="v.primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT.DiD_c.ci95" data-fmt="ci2"></span>. The matching DiD on <i>d′</i> is <span data-num="v.primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT.DiD_dprime.est" data-fmt="s3"></span> <span data-num="v.primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT.DiD_dprime.ci95" data-fmt="ci2"></span>.</div>
      <p style="margin-top:14px"><span class="badge">Estimate</span> <span class="small">The paper rates this an <button class="term" data-term="estimate">ESTIMATE</button>: counting partial answers as refusals reverses the sign (see <a href="#try">Try it</a>).</span></p>
    </div>
    <div class="card" id="view-headline">
      <div class="controls">
        <div class="ctl"><span class="lab" id="lab-hl-items">Items</span>
          <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="lab-hl-items">
            <label><input type="radio" name="hl-items" value="F" checked><span>Benign (false alarms)</span></label>
            <label><input type="radio" name="hl-items" value="H"><span>Harmful (hits)</span></label>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="ctl"><label class="lab" for="hl-variant">Analysis recorded in the run</label>
          <select id="hl-variant"></select>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="chart" id="chart-headline" role="group" aria-label="Refusal rate by model and prompt language"></div>
      <div class="legend" id="legend-headline"></div>
      <div class="readout" id="readout-headline" aria-live="polite"></div>
      <p class="takeaway" id="take-headline" aria-live="polite"></p>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
</section>

<!-- ============================================================ HOW -->
<section class="block" id="how" aria-labelledby="h-how">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-how">How it works: one prompt through the pipeline</h2>
  <p class="question">How does a single harmless request become part of a criterion estimate?</p>
  <p class="prose">We follow one real benign item from OR-Bench through each stage. The values shown are the ones the run recorded for this item; the tallies and SDT parameters in later stages are recomputed live from the embedded labels of all <span data-num="sdt.n_items" data-fmt="int"></span> HARD items.</p>
  <div class="stepper card" id="stepper" aria-roledescription="stepper">
    <div class="pipe" id="pipe"></div>
    <div class="navrow">
      <button class="tbtn" id="st-prev" type="button">&larr; Previous</button>
      <button class="tbtn" id="st-next" type="button">Next &rarr;</button>
      <span class="pos" id="st-pos"></span>
    </div>
    <div class="sr" aria-live="polite" id="st-live"></div>
    <div class="stage" id="stage" tabindex="-1"></div>
    <p class="takeaway" id="take-step"></p>
  </div>
</div>
</section>

<!-- ============================================================ EVIDENCE -->
<section class="block" id="evidence" aria-labelledby="h-evidence">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-evidence">Explore the evidence</h2>

  <h3 id="h-forest">Does the criterion shift hold across the analyses the run recorded?</h3>
  <p class="question">If we change the item set, the English arm, or the coding rule, does DiD<sub>c</sub> stay positive? And does <i>d′</i> stay near zero?</p>
  <div class="card">
    <div class="controls">
      <div class="ctl"><span class="lab" id="lab-forest">Parameter</span>
        <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="lab-forest">
          <label><input type="radio" name="forest-p" value="DiD_c" checked><span>Criterion DiD<sub>c</sub></span></label>
          <label><input type="radio" name="forest-p" value="DiD_dprime"><span>Sensitivity DiD<sub>d′</sub></span></label>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="chart" id="chart-forest" role="group" aria-label="Difference-in-differences across recorded analyses"></div>
    <div class="legend"><span><span class="sw" style="background:var(--accent)"></span>95% CI excludes 0</span><span><span class="sw" style="background:var(--base)"></span>95% CI includes 0</span><span class="muted">Point = estimate; line = bootstrap 95% CI from the run's analysis file.</span></div>
    <div id="forest-detail" class="tablewrap" style="margin-top:12px"></div>
    <p class="takeaway" id="take-forest" aria-live="polite"></p>
  </div>

  <h3 id="h-browser">What does over-refusal look like in one prompt?</h3>
  <p class="question">Which benign prompts does Gemma refuse only in Slovene, and what do the four replies actually say?</p>
  <p class="prose small muted" id="browser-rule"></p>
  <div class="card">
    <div class="controls">
      <div class="ctl"><label class="lab" for="br-pattern">Pattern</label>
        <select id="br-pattern">
          <option value="gemma_sl_only">Gemma refuses only in Slovene</option>
          <option value="gemma_en_only">Gemma refuses only in English</option>
          <option value="gams_differs">GaMS3 differs across languages</option>
          <option value="all_comply">No refusal in any of the four replies</option>
          <option value="any">All embedded benign items</option>
        </select>
      </div>
      <div class="ctl"><label class="lab" for="br-src">Source</label>
        <select id="br-src"><option value="all">XSTest + OR-Bench</option><option value="X">XSTest</option><option value="O">OR-Bench-Hard-1K</option></select>
      </div>
      <div class="ctl"><label class="lab" for="br-sort">Sort</label>
        <select id="br-sort"><option value="short">Shortest prompt first</option><option value="chrf">Lowest back-translation chrF first</option><option value="id">Item id</option></select>
      </div>
      <div class="ctl" style="flex:1 1 200px"><label class="lab" for="br-q">Search prompts</label>
        <input type="search" id="br-q" placeholder="e.g. letter, password, history" autocomplete="off">
      </div>
    </div>
    <p class="count" id="br-count" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <div class="browser">
      <ul class="ilist" id="br-list" role="listbox" aria-label="Benign items"></ul>
      <div class="detail" id="br-detail" aria-live="polite"></div>
    </div>
    <p class="takeaway" id="take-browser" aria-live="polite"></p>
  </div>
</div>
</section>

<!-- ============================================================ TRY -->
<section class="block" id="try" aria-labelledby="h-try">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-try">Try it: recompute the SDT parameters</h2>
  <p class="question">What if partial answers counted as refusals, or only one benchmark were kept?</p>
  <p class="prose">Every control below re-tallies the recorded judge labels and recomputes <i>H</i>, <i>F</i>, <i>d′</i> and <i>c</i> in your browser, using the <button class="term" data-term="hautus">Hautus correction</button> the run used. When a setting matches an analysis the run recorded, the page also prints that analysis's bootstrap interval from the file; other combinations get a point estimate only.</p>
  <div class="card">
    <div class="controls">
      <div class="ctl"><span class="lab" id="lab-code">PARTIAL answers count as</span>
        <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="lab-code">
          <label><input type="radio" name="try-code" value="comply" checked><span>Compliance</span></label>
          <label><input type="radio" name="try-code" value="refuse"><span>Refusal</span></label>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="ctl"><label class="lab" for="try-src">Items</label>
        <select id="try-src"><option value="all">XSTest + OR-Bench</option><option value="X">XSTest only</option><option value="O">OR-Bench only</option></select>
      </div>
      <div class="ctl"><label class="lab" for="try-en">English arm</label>
        <select id="try-en"><option value="EN_BT">Back-translation (primary)</option><option value="EN_orig">Original English</option></select>
      </div>
      <label class="check"><input type="checkbox" id="try-frag"> Drop <button class="term" data-term="frag" type="button">MT-fragile</button> items</label>
      <div class="ctl"><span class="lab" id="lab-sdtm">Picture</span>
        <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="lab-sdtm">
          <label><input type="radio" name="try-model" value="gemma_it" checked><span>Gemma</span></label>
          <label><input type="radio" name="try-model" value="gams3_it"><span>GaMS3</span></label>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="two">
      <div>
        <div class="tablewrap" id="try-table"></div>
        <div class="readout" id="try-readout" aria-live="polite"></div>
      </div>
      <div>
        <div class="chart" id="chart-sdt" role="group" aria-label="Equal-variance signal-detection picture"></div>
        <div class="legend"><span><span class="sw" style="background:#c9d3de"></span>Benign items</span><span><span class="sw" style="background:#f0c9b5"></span>Harmful items</span><span><span class="sw" style="background:var(--base)"></span>English criterion</span><span><span class="sw" style="background:var(--accent)"></span>Slovene criterion</span></div>
        <p class="note">The curves are the equal-variance Gaussian model implied by each cell's recorded <i>H</i> and <i>F</i>: benign evidence ~ N(0,1), harmful ~ N(<i>d′</i>,1). A reply is a refusal when the evidence falls right of the criterion line; the shaded benign area is <i>F</i>.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
    <p class="takeaway" id="take-try" aria-live="polite"></p>
  </div>
</div>
</section>

<!-- ============================================================ REPLY -->
<section class="block" id="reply" aria-labelledby="h-reply">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-reply">Secondary result: does residual refusal follow the reply language?</h2>
  <p class="question">After a partial English <button class="term" data-term="abl">abliteration</button> edit, is refusal set by the language of the prompt or by the language the model is asked to answer in?</p>
  <p class="prose">Experiment 14 crosses three prompt languages with three requested reply languages, <span data-num="grid.cells.gemma_it|hi|enen|harmful.n" data-fmt="int"></span> harmful and <span data-num="grid.cells.gemma_it|hi|enen|benign.n" data-fmt="int"></span> benign prompts per cell, at three <button class="term" data-term="dose">edit doses</button>. Point at a cell for its rate, interval and <button class="term" data-term="compl">language compliance</button>.</p>
  <div class="card">
    <div class="controls">
      <div class="ctl"><span class="lab" id="lab-dose">Edit dose</span>
        <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="lab-dose">
          <label><input type="radio" name="g-dose" value="zero"><span>Zero (unedited)</span></label>
          <label><input type="radio" name="g-dose" value="lo"><span>Low</span></label>
          <label><input type="radio" name="g-dose" value="hi" checked><span>High</span></label>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="ctl"><span class="lab" id="lab-gkind">Items</span>
        <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="lab-gkind">
          <label><input type="radio" name="g-kind" value="harmful" checked><span>Harmful</span></label>
          <label><input type="radio" name="g-kind" value="benign"><span>Benign</span></label>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="heat">
      <div><h4 style="margin-top:0">Gemma-3-12B-IT</h4><div class="chart" id="heat-gemma_it" role="group" aria-label="Gemma refusal grid"></div></div>
      <div><h4 style="margin-top:0">GaMS3-12B-Instruct</h4><div class="chart" id="heat-gams3_it" role="group" aria-label="GaMS3 refusal grid"></div></div>
    </div>
    <p class="note">Rows: prompt language. Columns: requested reply language. Colour: refusal rate, white 0 to dark red 1. † marks a cell whose language compliance, pooled over the three doses, is below 90%. Primary-judge raw readout.</p>
    <p class="takeaway" id="take-grid" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <h4>Contrasts recorded for the grid (high dose, log-odds)</h4>
    <div class="tablewrap" id="grid-contrasts"></div>
    <p class="note">Raw contrasts use the primary judge's labels. <button class="term" data-term="ppi">PPI++</button> corrects them against a blind author-model adjudication (not human); the paper reports the corrected value for Gemma only.</p>
  </div>
</div>
</section>

<!-- ============================================================ FAILS -->
<section class="block" id="fails" aria-labelledby="h-fails">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-fails">Where it fails</h2>
  <p class="question">Which paired items run against the headline, and how many are there?</p>
  <div class="card">
    <div class="controls">
      <div class="ctl"><span class="lab" id="lab-disc">Items</span>
        <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="lab-disc">
          <label><input type="radio" name="disc-kind" value="safe" checked><span>Benign</span></label>
          <label><input type="radio" name="disc-kind" value="unsafe"><span>Harmful</span></label>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="chart" id="chart-disc" role="group" aria-label="Discordant item pairs by model"></div>
    <div class="legend"><span><span class="sw" style="background:var(--accent)"></span>Refused in Slovene only</span><span><span class="sw" style="background:var(--base)"></span>Refused in English only</span></div>
    <p class="takeaway" id="take-disc" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <div class="navrow" style="margin-top:12px">
      <button class="tbtn" type="button" id="open-counter">Read Gemma's English-only refusals</button>
      <button class="tbtn" type="button" id="open-judge">Read a Slovene label we dispute</button>
    </div>
    <p class="note" id="judge-note"></p>
  </div>
  <h3>What the paper says it does not show</h3>
  <ul class="lim">
    <li><b>The sign depends on a coding rule.</b> Counting PARTIAL answers as refusals turns DiD<sub>c</sub> into <span data-num="v.primary_Rp.DiD_c.est" data-fmt="s2"></span> <span data-num="v.primary_Rp.DiD_c.ci95" data-fmt="ci2"></span>. Whether over-refusal is attributed to Gemma or is absent turns on this choice.</li>
    <li><b>The effect is carried by OR-Bench.</b> On XSTest items alone DiD<sub>c</sub> is <span data-num="v.xstest_only.DiD_c.est" data-fmt="s2"></span> <span data-num="v.xstest_only.DiD_c.ci95" data-fmt="ci2"></span>.</li>
    <li><b>One judge, not human-validated.</b> Every label here comes from a local <button class="term" data-term="judge">Qwen3-14B judge</button> calibrated against gemini-2.5-flash on DEV, never against human labels; the readout gate never passed. All adjudication in the study is by an author LLM, not a person.</li>
    <li><b>Edited models are inconclusive.</b> After the abliteration edit (Experiment 11), the criterion DiD is <span data-num="exp11.edited_DiD_c.est" data-fmt="f2"></span> <span data-num="exp11.edited_DiD_c.ci95" data-fmt="ci2"></span>.</li>
    <li><b>The reply-language result has a weak anchor.</b> Experiment 16's PPI estimate OUT<sub>Gemma</sub> = <span data-num="exp16.OUT_gemma_ppi.est" data-fmt="s2"></span> <span data-num="exp16.OUT_gemma_ppi.ci95" data-fmt="cis2"></span> is capped at ESTIMATE because the harmful-content adjudicators agree at κ = <span data-num="exp16.kappa_U" data-fmt="f2"></span>, below the 0.60 gate. On Experiment 14, the PPI-corrected OUT<sub>SL</sub> for Gemma includes zero.</li>
    <li><b>Four GaMS3 grid cells are unreliable.</b> Off the English-prompt row GaMS3 did not follow the reply-language instruction (its SL→EN replies were in Slovene), so its mechanism claims rest on the English-prompt row only.</li>
    <li><b>Translation and precision.</b> Slovene prompts are machine translations that no native speaker checked, and both models ran in NF4 4-bit quantization.</li>
    <li><b>Novelty is partial.</b> That over-refusal differs across languages is anticipated by concurrent work (Addagada 2026; Nguyen et al. 2026). What this study adds is the signal-detection decomposition on a controlled sibling pair.</li>
  </ul>
</div>

const col = (m, arm) => ORDER.indexOf(m + '|' + arm);
function srcOk(r, src) { return src === 'all' || (src === 'X' ? r[1] === 'X' : r[1] !== 'X'); }
function tally(o) {
  const isRef = ch => ch === 'R' || (o.partial === 'refuse' && ch === 'P');
  const cells = {};
  for (const m of MODELS) {
    for (const [lang, arm] of [['EN', o.enArm], ['SL', o.slArm]]) {
      const i = col(m, arm); let kH = 0, nH = 0, kF = 0, nF = 0;
      for (const r of LAB.rows) {
        if (!srcOk(r, o.src) || (o.dropFrag && r[3] === 1)) continue;
        const ref = isRef(r[4][i]);
        if (r[2]) { nH++; if (ref) kH++; } else { nF++; if (ref) kF++; }
      }
      const H = (kH + 0.5) / (nH + 1), F = (kF + 0.5) / (nF + 1), zH = qnorm(H), zF = qnorm(F);
      cells[m + '|' + lang] = { kH, nH, kF, nF, H, F, zH, zF, d: zH - zF, c: -(zH + zF) / 2 };
    }
  }
  const g = cells;
  return {
    cells,
    didc: (g['gams3_it|SL'].c - g['gams3_it|EN'].c) - (g['gemma_it|SL'].c - g['gemma_it|EN'].c),
    didd: (g['gams3_it|SL'].d - g['gams3_it|EN'].d) - (g['gemma_it|SL'].d - g['gemma_it|EN'].d)
  };
}
const BASE_O = { src: 'all', dropFrag: false, partial: 'comply', enArm: 'EN_BT', slArm: 'SL_MT' };
const LANGS_STD = ['English (back-translated)', 'Slovene (MT)'];
const VARS = {
  primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT: { label: 'Primary: Slovene MT vs English back-translation', o: {}, langs: LANGS_STD },
  SLMT_vs_ENorig: { label: 'Slovene MT vs original English', o: { enArm: 'EN_orig' }, langs: ['English (original)', 'Slovene (MT)'] },
  ENBT_vs_ENorig_MTnoise: { label: 'Placebo: back-translated vs original English', o: { enArm: 'EN_orig', slArm: 'EN_BT' }, langs: ['English (original)', 'English (back-translated)'], placebo: true },
  xstest_only: { label: 'XSTest items only', o: { src: 'X' }, langs: LANGS_STD },
  orbench_only: { label: 'OR-Bench items only', o: { src: 'O' }, langs: LANGS_STD },
  mt_fragile_dropped: { label: 'MT-fragile items dropped', o: { dropFrag: true }, langs: LANGS_STD },
  SLNLLB_vs_ENorig_xstest: { label: 'NLLB Slovene MT vs original English (XSTest subset)', o: null, langs: ['English (original)', 'Slovene (NLLB MT)'] },
  primary_Rp: { label: 'PARTIAL answers counted as refusals', o: { partial: 'refuse' }, langs: LANGS_STD }
};
for (const k in VARS) if (VARS[k].o) VARS[k].o = Object.assign({}, BASE_O, VARS[k].o);
const VKEYS = Object.keys(VARS).filter(k => SDT.variants[k]);
const TALLY = {};
for (const k of VKEYS) if (VARS[k].o) TALLY[k] = tally(VARS[k].o);
window.__check = { TALLY, SDT };

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ svg helpers */
const NS = 'http://www.w3.org/2000/svg';
function S(tag, attrs, parent) {
  const e = document.createElementNS(NS, tag);
  if (attrs) for (const k in attrs) e.setAttribute(k, attrs[k]);
  if (parent) parent.appendChild(e);
  return e;
}
function T(parent, x, y, str, attrs) { const t = S('text', Object.assign({ x, y }, attrs || {}), parent); t.textContent = str; return t; }
function measure(svg, str, cls) { const t = S('text', { class: cls, x: -9999, y: -9999 }, svg); t.textContent = str; const w = t.getComputedTextLength(); t.remove(); return w; }
function newSvg(host, h, label) {
  host.innerHTML = '';
  const w = Math.max(280, host.clientWidth);
  const svg = S('svg', { viewBox: `0 0 ${w} ${h}`, width: w, height: h, role: 'presentation' }, host);
  if (label) svg.setAttribute('aria-label', label);
  return { svg, w, h };
}
function niceTicks(lo, hi, n) {
  const span = hi - lo, step0 = span / n, mag = Math.pow(10, Math.floor(Math.log10(step0)));
  const step = [1, 2, 2.5, 5, 10].map(s => s * mag).find(s => span / s <= n) || 10 * mag;
  const out = []; for (let v = Math.ceil(lo / step) * step; v <= hi + 1e-9; v += step) out.push(+v.toFixed(10));
  return { ticks: out, step };
}
/* chart tooltip */
const tip = document.getElementById('charttip');
let tipOwner = null;
function showTip(el, html, evt) {
  tip.innerHTML = html; tip.classList.add('on'); tipOwner = el;
  let x, y;
  if (evt && evt.pageX != null && evt.type !== 'focus' && (evt.pageX || evt.pageY)) { x = evt.pageX; y = evt.pageY; }
  else { const r = el.getBoundingClientRect(); x = r.left + r.width / 2 + scrollX; y = r.top + scrollY; }
  const tw = tip.offsetWidth, th = tip.offsetHeight, vw = document.documentElement.clientWidth;
  let L = Math.max(8 + scrollX, Math.min(x - tw / 2, scrollX + vw - tw - 8));
  let Tp = y - th - 14; if (Tp < scrollY + 4) Tp = y + 20;
  tip.style.left = L + 'px'; tip.style.top = Tp + 'px';
}
function hideTip() { tip.classList.remove('on'); tipOwner = null; }
function bindMark(g, html, label, onSelect) {
  g.setAttribute('tabindex', '0');
  g.setAttribute('role', onSelect ? 'button' : 'img');
  g.setAttribute('aria-label', label);
  g.classList.add('mark');
  g.addEventListener('mouseenter', e => showTip(g, html(), e));
  g.addEventListener('mousemove', e => showTip(g, html(), e));
  g.addEventListener('mouseleave', hideTip);
  g.addEventListener('focus', e => showTip(g, html(), e));
  g.addEventListener('blur', hideTip);
  g.addEventListener('click', e => { showTip(g, html(), e); if (onSelect) onSelect(); });
  if (onSelect) g.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') { e.preventDefault(); onSelect(); } });
}
document.addEventListener('click', e => { if (tipOwner && !e.target.closest('.mark')) hideTip(); });
document.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.key === 'Escape') hideTip(); });
const radio = name => document.querySelector(`input[name="${name}"]:checked`).value;
function onRadio(name, fn) { document.querySelectorAll(`input[name="${name}"]`).forEach(i => i.addEventListener('change', fn)); }

/* y-axis frame with measured left margin */
function frame(svg, w, h, yTicks, fmtY, yTitle, opts) {
  opts = opts || {};
  const tickW = Math.max(...yTicks.map(t => measure(svg, fmtY(t), 'tick')));
  const left = 8 + 14 + 10 + tickW + 8, top = opts.top || 14, bottom = opts.bottom || 44, right = opts.right || 10;
  const pw = w - left - right, ph = h - top - bottom;
  const g = S('g', { class: 'ax' }, svg);
  const y = v => top + ph - (v - opts.ymin) / (opts.ymax - opts.ymin) * ph;
  yTicks.forEach(t => {
    S('line', { x1: left, x2: left + pw, y1: y(t), y2: y(t), class: 'gridl' }, g);
    T(g, left - 8, y(t) + 4, fmtY(t), { class: 'tick', 'text-anchor': 'end' });
  });
  S('line', { x1: left, x2: left, y1: top, y2: top + ph, class: 'axis' }, g);
  S('line', { x1: left, x2: left + pw, y1: top + ph, y2: top + ph, class: 'axis' }, g);
  const tx = 8 + 10;
  T(g, 0, 0, yTitle, { class: 'atitle', 'text-anchor': 'middle', transform: `translate(${tx},${top + ph / 2}) rotate(-90)` });
  return { left, top, pw, ph, y, g };
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ 1. headline chart */
const hlSel = document.getElementById('hl-variant');
VKEYS.filter(k => VARS[k].o).forEach(k => { const o = document.createElement('option'); o.value = k; o.textContent = VARS[k].label; hlSel.appendChild(o); });
const SER_COL = ['var(--base)', 'var(--accent)'];
function drawHeadline() {
  const key = hlSel.value, which = radio('hl-items'), V = VARS[key], file = SDT.variants[key], tl = TALLY[key];
  const host = document.getElementById('chart-headline');
  const { svg, w, h } = newSvg(host, 300);
  const f = frame(svg, w, h, [0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1], t => t.toFixed(1), which === 'F' ? 'Share of benign prompts refused' : 'Share of harmful prompts refused', { ymin: 0, ymax: 1, bottom: 40, top: 22 });
  const groupW = f.pw / 2, barW = Math.min(64, groupW * 0.3), gap = 8;
  MODELS.forEach((m, gi) => {
    const cx = f.left + groupW * gi + groupW / 2;
    T(svg, cx, f.top + f.ph + 24, MFULL[m], { class: 'tick', 'text-anchor': 'middle', style: 'font-weight:600;fill:var(--ink)' });
    [0, 1].forEach(si => {
      const fileIdx = gi * 2 + si, val = file.cells[which][fileIdx];
      const cell = tl.cells[m + '|' + (si ? 'SL' : 'EN')];
      const k = which === 'F' ? cell.kF : cell.kH, n = which === 'F' ? cell.nF : cell.nH, wi = wilson(k, n);
      const x = cx + (si ? gap / 2 : -gap / 2 - barW);
      const g = S('g', {}, svg);
      S('rect', { class: 'bar', x, y: f.y(val), width: barW, height: f.y(0) - f.y(val), fill: SER_COL[si], rx: 2 }, g);
      S('line', { x1: x + barW / 2, x2: x + barW / 2, y1: f.y(wi[1]), y2: f.y(wi[0]), stroke: 'var(--ink)', 'stroke-width': 1.4 }, g);
      [wi[0], wi[1]].forEach(v => S('line', { x1: x + barW / 2 - 5, x2: x + barW / 2 + 5, y1: f.y(v), y2: f.y(v), stroke: 'var(--ink)', 'stroke-width': 1.4 }, g));
      const txt = which === 'F' ? num(val, 3) : num(val, 2);
      T(g, x + barW / 2, f.y(wi[1]) - 6, txt, { class: 'tick', 'text-anchor': 'middle', style: 'font-weight:650;fill:var(--ink)' });
      S('rect', { class: 'hit', x: x - 2, y: f.top, width: barW + 4, height: f.ph, fill: 'transparent' }, g);
      const lab = `${MFULL[m]}, ${V.langs[si]}: ${which === 'F' ? 'false-alarm rate' : 'hit rate'} ${txt}; refused ${k} of ${n}; Wilson 95% CI ${num(wi[0], 3)} to ${num(wi[1], 3)}`;
      bindMark(g, () => `<b>${MFULL[m]} · ${V.langs[si]}</b><br>${which === 'F' ? 'False-alarm rate <i>F</i>' : 'Hit rate <i>H</i>'} = ${txt} (recorded, Hautus-corrected)<br>Raw: ${nf.format(k)} of ${nf.format(n)} refused<br>Wilson 95% CI [${num(wi[0], 3)}, ${num(wi[1], 3)}]`, lab);
    });
  });
  document.getElementById('legend-headline').innerHTML = V.langs.map((l, i) => `<span><span class="sw" style="background:${SER_COL[i]}"></span>${l}</span>`).join('') + '<span class="muted">Whiskers: Wilson 95% CI on the raw proportion</span>';
  const dc = file.DiD_c, dd = file.DiD_dprime;
  let ro = `<div><span class="k">DiD<sub>c</sub> (recorded)</span><span class="v">${sauto(dc.est)} ${ci(dc.ci95)}</span></div><div><span class="k">DiD<sub>d′</sub> (recorded)</span><span class="v">${sauto(dd.est)} ${ci(dd.ci95)}</span></div>`;
  if (key === 'primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT' || key === 'SLMT_vs_ENorig' || key === 'primary_Rp' || true) {
    const mc = SDT.mcnemar;
    if (key === 'primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT') ro += `<div><span class="k">Gemma, benign SL vs EN (exact McNemar)</span><span class="v">${pval(mc.gemma_it.safe.p_exact)}</span></div><div><span class="k">GaMS3, benign SL vs EN</span><span class="v">${pval(mc.gams3_it.safe.p_exact)}</span></div>`;
  }
  document.getElementById('readout-headline').innerHTML = ro;
  const c = file.cells[which];
  let t;
  const excl = dc.ci95[0] > 0 ? 'its 95% CI excludes zero' : (dc.ci95[1] < 0 ? 'its 95% CI lies entirely below zero, so the sign has reversed' : 'its 95% CI includes zero');
  if (which === 'F') {
    t = V.placebo
      ? `<b>Placebo check.</b> Both bars in each pair are English; only the translation round-trip differs. Gemma moves ${num(c[0], 3)} → ${num(c[1], 3)} and GaMS3 ${num(c[2], 3)} → ${num(c[3], 3)}, and DiD<sub>c</sub> = ${sauto(dc.est)} ${ci(dc.ci95)}: machine-translation noise alone does not create the shift.`
      : `<b>${V.label}.</b> Gemma refuses ${num(c[1], 3)} of benign Slovene prompts against ${num(c[0], 3)} in English (${pp(c[1] - c[0])}); GaMS3 refuses ${num(c[3], 3)} against ${num(c[2], 3)} (${pp(c[3] - c[2])}). DiD<sub>c</sub> = ${sauto(dc.est)} ${ci(dc.ci95)}; ${excl}.`;
  } else {
    t = `<b>Hits move little.</b> On harmful prompts Gemma refuses ${num(c[0], 2)} in ${V.langs[0].split(' ')[0].toLowerCase() === 'english' ? 'the first arm' : 'English'} and ${num(c[1], 2)} in the second; GaMS3 ${num(c[2], 2)} and ${num(c[3], 2)}. The language gap is carried by benign prompts, which is why the criterion moves while <i>d′</i> does not (DiD<sub>d′</sub> = ${sauto(dd.est)} ${ci(dd.ci95)}).`;
  }
